# A-to-Mind

> Verse by A-to-Mind does whatever anyone asks: ask for something and it appears. Nothing is shown until someone asks, and there is nothing to sign up for.

## What you can ask for today
- Things on the stage: a clock, timer, counter, sticky note, notepad, list, calculator, shape, image or link card ("make a 5 minute timer", "draw a circle", "add a sticky that says hi"). They stay in your browser across visits.
- Changes to the stage: "make it blue", "make everything bigger", "clear", "undo".
- Layers and groups: "bring the clock to the front", "send the note to the back", "group the clock and the note" (drag one and they move together), "move the group to the top left", "make the group bigger", "bring the group to the front", "ungroup".
- Labels and arrows: "label the clock kitchen", "put a label on the timer that says pasta", "add a label that says to do", "draw an arrow from the clock to the note" (it follows them when you drag), "connect the timer to the counter", "draw an arrow from kitchen to groceries" (by label), "remove the arrows", "remove the labels".
- Books, TV, teams and holidays: "books by Octavia Butler", "tv show Severance", "nba team Celtics", "public holidays in Japan".
- Floating pages: the weather ("weather in Tokyo"), UV index ("UV index in Miami", "should I wear sunscreen in Phoenix"), recent earthquakes ("earthquakes near Tokyo", "recent earthquakes"), pollen and allergy levels ("pollen in Paris", "allergy forecast in Berlin"), bedtimes and wake-up times by sleep cycles ("if I wake up at 7am when should I go to sleep", "sleep calculator", "how much sleep does a teenager need"), a pregnancy due date or how far along you are ("due date if my last period was March 1", "my due date is June 1 how far along am I", "due date calculator"), a fertile window, ovulation day or next period ("when am I ovulating if my last period was March 1", "when is my next period if my last period was Sept 20", "ovulation calculator"), a period log kept only in your browser that learns your own cycle ("my period started today", "show my period log", "how long is my cycle", "is my period late"; then "when am I ovulating" needs no date), the time anywhere ("time in Tokyo", "3pm London to Tokyo", "sunset in Paris"), a street map ("map of Lisbon", "where is Kyoto"), a translation ("translate hello to Spanish"), a calculation or conversion ("5 miles in km", "100 usd in eur"), a loan payment ("monthly payment on a $250000 mortgage at 6.5% for 30 years"), trip fuel ("gas cost for 320 miles at 28 mpg $3.59 a gallon"), a tip or bill split ("20% tip on 45", "split $85 three ways with 20% tip"), daily calories, protein and water for you ("how many calories should i eat a day", "calories for a 30 year old male 5'10 180 lbs moderately active", "how much protein do i need if i weigh 180 pounds", "how much water should i drink a day", "calorie calculator"; then change one thing: "what if i'm very active", "to lose 1 pound a week", "i'm a woman", "and protein"), your target heart rate and five training zones ("what is my target heart rate", "heart rate zones for a 40 year old", "fat burning heart rate for a 35 year old", "my resting heart rate is 60" for zones on your heart rate reserve, "what is a normal resting heart rate", "heart rate zone calculator"), paint or flooring for a room ("how much paint do i need for a 12x14 room", "how many 12x24 tiles for a 10x12 floor", "how much carpet for a 12x14 room", "paint calculator"), wallpaper rolls or drywall sheets for the same room ("how many rolls of wallpaper for a 12x14 room", "how many sheets of drywall for a 12x14 room and the ceiling", "wallpaper calculator"), everything for one room on one card with a price per line and the total ("redo a 12x14 room", "paint and carpet a 12x14 room at $40 a gallon", "wallpaper the walls and paint the ceiling of a 12x12 room", or "the whole room" after any of those cards), or a page about almost anything ("what is a black hole"), with its source linked.
- Keep a page as a card with "keep this"; "call this ...", "take this off" and "same again" work on it.
- Board games standing in 3D in the void, each with its own card beside it: "games" opens a 3D game rack (tap a box to play), "play go" (two players, 9×9), "play monopoly" (you against Verse, with the reasons for every choice Verse makes), "play battleship" (Verse's fleet stays hidden; every shot it takes says why), "play poker" (Texas Hold'em for play money; Verse never sees your cards and shows its odds), "play fireworks" (a co-op card game: you and Verse on the same side, each seeing only the other's cards), "play chess", "play checkers", "play othello", "play tic tac toe", "play mancala", "play aggravation".
- Your own look: "make my void deep blue", "add stars", "quieter font", "reset my void".
- Saving money: what saving each month grows to ("how much will I have if I save 200 a month for 20 years at 7%"), how long a goal takes ("how long to save 50000 if I save 500 a month"), what a goal needs each month ("how much do I need to save a month to have 1 million in 30 years at 7%"), or a "savings calculator".
- Optional, never required: "remember me" keeps your stage, look and kept cards on every device with a passkey (no password, no email). Then "sign in" on another device, "am I signed in", "sign out", "forget me". Agents can't ask these for someone.
- Code review: "review my code" and paste it (any of 22 languages, GitHub workflows, Dockerfiles, Terraform): bugs, security holes and risky habits with line numbers, a fixed version where the fix is safe, then a closer read. For every pull request: the free GitHub Action `atomeam/void-loop/review@main` (a whole PR in about a second, inline one-click fixes, an optional merge gate); Verse Pro adds the AI closer read. Details and pricing: https://a-to-mind.com/code-review/
- Store: "what can I buy" lists everything Verse sells. https://a-to-mind.com/store/ has 3D models and printable minis with live 3D previews, Verse Pro, Code Review Pro and hands-on automation services: a cart, hosted checkout (Gumroad today, Stripe next; Verse never sees a card), signed 24-hour download links, Verse license keys and order lookup by email and order code.
- Hands-on services (ask Verse "what do you sell" for the card with live prices): a broken automation fixed with proof (https://a-to-mind.com/one-time-fix/), round-the-clock monitoring and repair (https://a-to-mind.com/keep-it-running/), a full review of every automation you run (https://a-to-mind.com/full-stack-audit/), your first automation built for you (https://a-to-mind.com/first-automation-setup/). Each page shows the live price from /api/catalog and links its Gumroad checkout.
- Fix pages: the common Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate and GitHub Actions errors (401, 403, 422, throttling and 429, turned-off or held Zaps, RateLimitError, ConnectionError, DataError, n8n webhook 404 and Google credential 401, Power Automate 429, GitHub Actions "Resource not accessible by integration"), each with what it means and the steps to fix it (https://a-to-mind.com/fix/).
- "menu" or "what can I do" lists every skill, clickable.

## Tool pages
Each tool is a page of its own, free, with nothing to sign up for and no ads; all of them on one page: https://a-to-mind.com/tools/. A link can carry the setting (https://a-to-mind.com/convert/?q=100+c+to+f, https://a-to-mind.com/time/?c=tokyo, https://a-to-mind.com/base64/?mode=decode), and each page's "Common asks" row shows the ones people want most. This list is written from lib/seo.js by tools/seo-pages.mjs.
<!-- tools -->
- Colour codes, shades and schemes: Type a colour as hex, RGB, HSL or a name and get it in every model, its nearest name, tints, shades and tones, five colour schemes and whether text on it can be read. Palettes made from it, your own saved palettes, colour-blind views and the 216 web-safe colours. Nothing sent anywhere. https://a-to-mind.com/color/
- CSS gradient generator: Make a linear, radial or conic CSS gradient from colour stops, name it, save it as your own preset on your device, pick colours from the screen, and copy its CSS. Nothing sent anywhere. https://a-to-mind.com/gradient/
- Wheel of names: Names, choices or pictures, spun on a fair wheel with the spin time you choose, confetti and a cheer for the winner, who can leave the wheel by itself; the winner is picked at random on your device. https://a-to-mind.com/wheel/
- Made-up people for testing: Made-up people by count, gender and 22 countries, with titles, names, addresses, two phones, dates of birth, passwords to your rules and pictures, as JSON, CSV, YAML, XML or SQL, from a seed you can repeat page by page. None of them is real. https://a-to-mind.com/random-user/
- Random number: A random number between two bounds, several at once, without repeats or sorted, with decimal places or in binary, octal or hex, plus a shuffled deck of cards dealt into hands and random dates and times; the number is on screen at once. https://a-to-mind.com/random/
- Flip a coin: Heads or tails from a coin that lands in under a second, with no ads and nothing to accept. https://a-to-mind.com/flip/
- Stopwatch and timer: A stopwatch with laps, a countdown timer with presets, your own saved timers and a choice of alarms, an interval timer (work and rest rounds in sets) and a chess clock with increment, kept on your device, working offline. https://a-to-mind.com/stopwatch/
- Word counter: Words, characters with and without spaces, sentences, paragraphs, pages, reading and speaking time and repeated phrases as you type, with a word goal, read aloud, earlier versions kept on your device and the limits your text fits. Nothing sent anywhere. https://a-to-mind.com/word-count/
- Binary, decimal, hex and octal converter: Type a number in binary, octal, decimal, hex or any base up to 36 and see it in all of them at once, exact at any size, fractions too (a repeating part in brackets), with its signed reading, its text and the working step by step. https://a-to-mind.com/base-converter/
- How secure is my password?: How long a password would take to guess, why, and what to change, worked out on your device: the password is never sent anywhere. https://a-to-mind.com/password-strength/
- Resize and compress a photo: Make a photo or signature an exact size in cm, mm, inches or pixels and under a size limit in KB, as a JPEG or a PDF, on your device: nothing is uploaded. https://a-to-mind.com/resize-image/
- Unit converter: Convert 52 kinds of unit, from length to torque, voltage, capacitance, density and typography, every unit of a kind at once, both ways, from exact definitions, with the formula and your choice of precision; type an ask like 100 c to f. https://a-to-mind.com/convert/
- Scientific calculator: Brackets, powers, roots, sin, cos and tan in degrees or radians, logs, factorial, percent, memory keys, a history kept on your device, unit conversion and keyboard input; exact display (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3); plus loan with an amortization schedule and chart, mortgage, compound interest, percentage, BMI and calorie calculators. Works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/calculator/
- Time zones: The current time in any city, a world clock of the places you pick, a time zone converter and a meeting planner, with daylight saving, from your browser’s own time-zone data. Works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/time/
- Base64 encode and decode: Encode text to Base64 and decode Base64 to text as you type, Base64 and Base64URL, with or without padding, exact for emoji and accents in 44 character sets; files of any size become Base64 and data: URLs on your device. Works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/base64/
- Password generator: Strong random passwords of 4 to 128 characters and passphrases of 3 to 10 words, made on your device, each with its exact entropy in bits and the time to crack. Nothing sent, works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/password/
- Scores: Live scores, final scores, schedules in your own time zone and standings for the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, MLS, Champions League, NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL and Formula 1, with box scores, team pages and favourite teams kept on your device. No ads, no betting. https://a-to-mind.com/scores/
- Sports: Browse 42 sports, search teams, events, venues and players across all of them in one box, see which athletes were born on this day, and read about the free read-only scores API. No ads, no betting, no account. https://a-to-mind.com/sports/
- Translate: Translate text between 100 languages with the language detected as you type: listen to the translation, speak instead of typing, read the text in a photo or from the camera, copy it, share a link that carries it, keep a history and saved phrases, and see them again offline. https://a-to-mind.com/translate/
- Recipes: Recipes by name or by what is in your fridge: every quantity scaled to your servings, cups to ml and °F to °C, one step at a time with timers to tap while you cook, a shopping list, a share link and a history on your device. A dozen classics work offline. https://a-to-mind.com/recipes/
- Markets: Quotes and charts for stocks, ETFs, indices, currencies and crypto by symbol or name: price, change, day range, 52 weeks, volume, a 1D to Max chart you can hover, the close on any day, a watchlist on your device, compare two symbols, top movers. Prices may be delayed. No ads, no account. https://a-to-mind.com/markets/
- Calendar: A calendar on your device: month, week and day views, events that repeat (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, chosen weekdays), reminders that fire on the device, invites as a link or an email with the .ics, import and export .ics, quick add in plain words, search and keyboard arrows. Nothing goes to a server; it works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/calendar/
- AI image generator: Free text to image: describe a picture, pick one of 15 styles (photo, cinematic, anime, cartoon, oil painting, watercolour, pixel art, 3D render, fantasy, comic, sketch and more) and a shape (square, portrait, landscape, wide), make up to four at a go, leave things out, keep a seed to make the same picture again, download, and keep a gallery on your device. No sign-up; real people and adult pictures are not made. https://a-to-mind.com/image/
- Generators: 27 random generators that run on your device: fantasy names, town names, band names, usernames, pet names, writing prompts, story prompts, D&D NPCs, haiku, limericks, superpowers, side quests and more. The same link always gives the same result, favourites are kept in the browser, and any result can be turned into a cartoon. Works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/generators/
- Notes: Notes and documents on your device: bold, italic, headings, lists, checklists, code and links, many documents, search across all of them, version history to preview and restore, word count, export to .md, .html and .txt, import, print, a share link and a note typed as one line. Nothing goes to a server; it works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/notes/
- News: Headlines from the BBC, the Guardian, NPR, Al Jazeera, DW and more in one calm list: the source and age on every story, the same story from several sources grouped with the list of who carries it, sections from world to sport and regions, search, topics and sources you follow, a read-later list, four languages, bigger text and a headlines-only view. Every story links to its source; no ads, no account; it opens offline with the last headlines. https://a-to-mind.com/news/
- Boards: anonymous image and text boards: Anonymous image and text boards anyone can start: make a board with a short code, post threads with a picture, reply with quotes and greentext, a catalog, an archive, tripcodes, sage, spoilers, search across every board, a thread watcher on your device and threads that update themselves. Pictures lose their hidden location data before they are kept. https://a-to-mind.com/boards/
- Metronome: A free online metronome from 20 to 400 BPM: tap tempo, every time signature from 2/4 to 12/8, an accent on each beat you can set strong, medium, soft or silent, subdivisions (eighths, triplets, sixteenths, swing), nine sounds, a voice count, a visual beat and pendulum, a practice timer, a speed trainer, silent bars and setlists. No account, no ads; it works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/metronome/
- Piano: A free online piano you play with the computer keyboard, the mouse, a touch screen or a MIDI keyboard: twelve instruments, a sustain pedal on the space bar, the computer key shown on each note, reverb, transpose, sheet music in plain letters with public-domain songs, and recording that turns your playing into a sheet. Made in your browser; no account, nothing to download. https://a-to-mind.com/piano/
- Tuner: A free online chromatic tuner that listens through your microphone and shows how many cents flat or sharp you are: guitar (standard, drop D, DADGAD, open tunings, 7-string), bass, ukulele, violin, viola, cello, mandolin and banjo presets, an adjustable A4 reference, reference tones and a pitch pipe. The sound never leaves your device. https://a-to-mind.com/tuner/
- BPM counter: A free BPM counter: tap any key or the button to the beat and get the tempo, averaged over your last taps, with half and double time, a reset after a pause, the length of every note value in milliseconds and Hz, the length of a song in bars, and the tempo of an audio file measured on your device. Nothing is uploaded. https://a-to-mind.com/bpm/
- Chords and scales: A free chord and scale finder for piano and guitar: the notes, piano keys and guitar fingerings of 28 chord types, the chord named from the notes you pick, every scale that holds them, 22 scales, the chords of any major or minor key with roman numerals and what they lead to, common progressions, the circle of fifths and a chord transposer. It plays what it shows. https://a-to-mind.com/chords/
- Music tools: Free music tools that run on your device: a metronome, an online piano, a tuner, a BPM counter and a chord and scale finder, your setlists of saved tempos (shared by link), a catalogue of tempo words, scales, chords, tunings and songs to play, and practice recommendations. No account, no ads, no subscription; it works offline. https://a-to-mind.com/music/
- Podcasts: Search millions of podcasts or paste any RSS link. Play with speed from 0.5x to 3x, skip back 15 and forward 30, a sleep timer, chapters, transcripts, a queue and your place saved per episode. Follow shows and see new episodes, save episodes for offline, import and export OPML. All kept on your device, no account. https://a-to-mind.com/podcasts/
- Weather: The weather now, the next 24 hours and 7 days ahead for any place, in °F and °C side by side, with sunrise and sunset, the weather service’s alerts and radar for the United States, and a link that carries the place. https://a-to-mind.com/weather/
- Every Verse tool: Every tool Verse has built, each a page of its own and all tied together: colours, chance, time, words and numbers, keys and pictures. Free, private, offline after one visit. https://a-to-mind.com/tools/
<!-- /tools -->

## Linking to an answer
- https://a-to-mind.com/?q=<ask> opens Verse and runs the ask, for example https://a-to-mind.com/?q=weather%20in%20Tokyo

## Notes for crawlers and agents
- Everything runs in the browser at https://a-to-mind.com. The one public API is code review: POST https://a-to-mind.com/api/review with {"code": ...} or {"diff": ...} returns findings (free); a Verse Pro key adds the closer read (https://a-to-mind.com/code-review/).
- The public API is described in OpenAPI 3.1 at https://a-to-mind.com/openapi.json (code review, the MCP endpoint, tools.json, the catalog, and each skill's health: proven, checked, tested or experiment, at /skills/families.json), found from https://a-to-mind.com/.well-known/api-catalog (RFC 9727).
- Browser agents with WebMCP (Chrome) find Verse's tools declared on the page itself (void_ask, void_stage, void_calculate, ...): each takes one plain-words ask and returns what appeared. The same list is at https://a-to-mind.com/tools.json.
- Earlier pages on this domain described a different product (workflow execution, treaties, ledgers). They are retired.
Ask "summon a sprite" for a roaming 3D friend in your own Verse; "send them away" clears it.
